channel.title: The Valley Times-News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Valley Times-News (valleytimes-news.com)

item.title: Protest movement reaches LaFayette
item.description: Incidents in Minnesota have sparked national protests as people react to recent acts of violence involving Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers. Similar acts of protest were discovered in LaFayette after a concerned citizen brought them to the attention of the Valley Times‑News.

item.title: Lanett approves several resolutions, hears update on airport activity
item.description: Lanett council OKs bid for new trash contract, cable and jet-fuel software deals, and a standard hangar lease agreement as traffic and fuel sales climb at Lanett Regional Airport.

item.title: Valley football players commit to the collegiate level
item.description: Valley High quarterback Caden Foreman is on his way to Miles College in Birmingham, and one of his favorite receivers, Aaden Johnson, is bound for Millsaps College in Jackson, Mississippi.

item.title: Spencer Newman commits to Murray State University
item.description: Chambers Academy’s Spencer Newman, who helped win three state titles, becomes the school’s first Division I football signee with his National Signing Day commitment to Murray State.

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - Dean Collins: From Wailing Tents to Trusting Hearts
item.description: Dean Collins connects Israel’s desert complaints, teen camp grumbling, and his years as a college president to explore trusting God’s provision when leadership burdens feel overwhelming.

item.title: Gooden selected to serve on HAPPI Health, Inc. Board of Directors
item.description: Valley native Tonarius Gooden has been selected to a three-year term on HAPPI Health, Inc.’s Board of Directors, supporting its mission to expand affordable, high-quality care in North Alabama.

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - Bill King: The Lunch Box Museum
item.description: Bill King visits Columbus, Georgia's world-famous Lunch Box Museum, home to some 5,000 vintage lunchboxes and seven small museums under one roof.

item.title: Wellstar West Georgia Medical Center earns multiple national awards from Healthgrades
item.description: Wellstar West Georgia Medical Center earns multiple 2025–2026 Healthgrades honors, including America’s 250 Best Hospitals, ranking among only five hospitals in Georgia at this level.

item.title: Black History Program to again celebrate students
item.description: The City of West Point is bringing back its Black History Program for the 23rd year on Tuesday, Feb. 24.

item.title: Community volunteers team up to distribute over 1,300 meals
item.description: Community volunteers and Valley groups teamed up with the Food Bank of East Alabama to distribute over 1,300 ready-to-eat meals to about 320 families in a single day.
